(e) Remote pilot licences shall be validated or converted in accordance
with the requirements of this part.
2.3.11.4  CATEGORY RATINGS
(a) When established, category ratings shall be for categories of
remotely piloted aircraft listed in Subsection 2.3.11.3 of this section.
(b) The holder of a remote pilot licence seeking additional category
ratings to be added to the existing licence shall meet the requirements of this
Part regarding remotely piloted aircraft system appropriate to the privileges
for which the category rating is sought.

2.3.11.5 CLASS AND TYPE RATINGS
(a) A class rating shall be established for remotely piloted aircraft and
associated remote pilot station certificated for single-remote pilot operation
which have comparable handling, performance, and characteristics, unless
a type rating is considered necessary by the Authority.

(b) A type rating shall be established for remotely piloted aircraft and
associated remote pilot station certificated for operation with a minimum crew
of at least two remote pilots or when considered necessary by the Authority.
Note: Where a common type rating is established, it will be only for
remotely piloted aircraft with similar characteristics in terms of operating
procedures, systems, and handling.
(c) When an applicant for a remote pilot licence demonstrates
competencies for the initial issue of a remote pilot licence, the category
and ratings appropriate to the class or type of remotely piloted aircraft and
associated remote pilot station remote pilot station used in the demonstration
shall be entered on that remote pilot licence.
(d) The levels of performance to be achieved to operate the class or
type of remotely piloted aircraft for which the ratings are issued shall be
publicly available.

2.3.11.6  CIRCUMSTANCES IN WHICH CLASS AND TYPE RATINGS
ARE REQUIRED
(a) A Contracting State having issued a remote pilot licence will not
permit the holder of such remote pilot licence to act either as remote Pilot-in-
command or as remote co-pilot of an remotely piloted aircraft and associated
remote pilot station unless the holder has received authorization as follows —

(1)  the appropriate class rating specified in Paragraph 2.3.11.5(a)
of this section; or

(2)  a type rating when required in accordance with the provisions
of Paragraph 2.3.11.5(b) of this section.

(i)  When a type rating is issued limiting the privileges to
act as remote co-pilot, or limiting the privileges to act as
remote pilot only during the cruise phase of the flight, such
limitation shall be endorsed on the rating.

(ii) When a class rating is issued limiting the privileges to act
as remote pilot only during the cruise phase of the flight,
such limitation shall be endorsed on the rating.
(b) For the purpose of training, testing, or specific special-purpose
non-revenue flights, special authorization may be provided in writing to the
remote pilot licence holder by the Authority in place of issuing the class or
type rating in accordance with Paragraph 2.3.11.6(a) of this subsection. This
authorization shall be limited in validity to the time needed to complete the
specific flight.

2.3.11.7 REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ISSUE OF CLASS AND TYPE
RATINGS
(a) The applicant for a remote pilot licence shall have demonstrated the
competencies required for the safe operation of an remotely piloted aircraft
of the class for which the rating is sought.

(b) Type rating as required by 2.3.11.5 of this section —

(1)  the applicant for a remote pilot licence shall have—

(i)  gained, under appropriate supervision, experience in the
applicable type of remotely piloted aircraft and associated
remote pilot station and/or flight simulation training device
in the following —

(A) normal flight procedures and manoeuvres during all
phases of flight;

(B)  abnormal and emergency procedures and manoeuvres
in the event of failures and malfunctions of equipment,
such as engine, command and control link, systems,
and airframe;

(C)  instrument procedures, including instrument
approach, missed approach, and landing procedures
under normal, abnormal, and emergency conditions,
including simulated engine failure;

(D) for the issue of an aeroplane category type rating, upset
prevention and recovery training; and
Note: The aeroplane upset prevention and recovery training may be
integrated in the type rating programme or may be conducted immediately
after, as an additional module.

(E)  procedures for crew incapacitation and crew
coordination, including allocation of remote pilot
tasks; crew cooperation and use of checklists;
Note: Attention is called to 2.3.11.9 of this section on the qualifications
required for remote pilots giving remotely piloted aircraft system training.

(ii)  Demonstrated the competencies required for the safe
operation of the applicable type of remotely piloted
aircraft and associated remote pilot station and shall have
demonstrated command and control link management skills
relevant to the duties of a remote Pilot-in-command or a
remote co-pilot, as applicable.

2.3.11.8  USE OF A FLIGHT SIMULATION TRAINING DEVICE
FOR ACQUISITION OF EXPERIENCE AND DEMONSTRATION
OF COMPETENCIES
(a)  The use of a flight simulation training device for acquiring the
required experience or performing any manoeuvre required during the
demonstration of competencies for the issue of a remote pilot licence or
rating shall be approved by the Authority, which will ensure that the flight
simulation training device used is appropriate to the task.

2.3.11.9  CIRCUMSTANCES IN WHICH AUTHORIZATION TO
CONDUCT REMOTE PILOT LICENCE TRAINING IS REQUIRED
(a) A Contracting State, having issued a remote pilot licence, will not
permit the holder thereof to carry out remote pilot licence training required
for the issue of a remote pilot licence or rating unless such holder has received
proper authorization from such Contracting State. Proper authorization shall
comprise —

(1) a remotely piloted aircraft system instructor rating on the holder’s
remote pilot licence; or

(2) the authority to act as an agent of an approved training organization
authorised by the Authority to carry out remote pilot licence
training; or

(3) a specific authorization granted by the Contracting State which
issued the remote pilot licence.
(b) A Contracting State will not permit a person to carry out remote pilot
licence training on a flight simulation training device required for the issue
of an remote pilot licence or rating unless such person holds or has held an
appropriate remote pilot licence or has appropriate remotely piloted aircraft
system training and flight experience and has received proper authorization
from such Contracting State.
2.3.11.10 CREDITING OF REMOTELY PILOTED AIRCRAFT
SYSTEM FLIGHT TIME
(a) A student remote pilot shall be entitled to be credited in full with all
solo and dual instruction remotely piloted aircraft system flight time towards
the total flight time required for the initial issue of a remote pilot licence.
(b) The holder of a remote pilot licence shall be entitled to be credited
in full with all dual instruction remotely piloted aircraft system flight time
towards the total remotely piloted aircraft system flight time required for a
remote Pilot-in-command upgrade.

(c) The holder of a remote pilot licence shall be entitled to be credited
in full with all solo or dual instruction remotely piloted aircraft system flight
time, in a new category of remotely piloted aircraft or for obtaining a new
rating, towards the total remotely piloted aircraft system flight time required
for that rating.
(d) The holder of a remote pilot licence, when acting as remote co-pilot
of an remotely piloted aircraft certificated for operation by a single remote
pilot, but required by a Contracting State to be operated with a remote co-
pilot, shall be entitled to be credited with not more than fifty per cent of
the remote co-pilot remotely piloted aircraft system flight time towards the
total remotely piloted aircraft system flight time required for a remote Pilot-
in-command upgrade. The Contracting State may authorise that remotely
piloted aircraft system flight time be credited in full towards the total remotely
piloted aircraft system flight time required if the remotely piloted aircraft
system is equipped to be operated by a remote co-pilot and is operated in a
multi-crew operation.
(e) The holder of a remote pilot licence, when acting as remote co-
pilot of an remotely piloted aircraft certificated to be operated with a remote
co-pilot, shall be entitled to be credited in full with this remotely piloted
aircraft system flight time towards the total remotely piloted aircraft system
flight time required for a remote Pilot-in-command upgrade.
(f) The holder of a remote pilot licence, when acting as remote Pilot-
in-command under supervision, shall be entitled to be credited in full with
this remotely piloted aircraft system flight time towards the total remotely
piloted aircraft system flight time required for a remote Pilot-in-command
upgrade.
(g) When applying for a new rating, the holder of a remote pilot
licence shall be entitled to be credited with remotely piloted aircraft system
flight time experience as an remote pilot of remotely piloted aircraft. The
Authority will determine whether such experience is acceptable and, if so,
the extent to which the experience requirements for the issue of a rating can
be reduced accordingly.
Note: The total remotely piloted aircraft system flight time required is
derived from the approved competency-based training programme.

2.3.11.11 LIMITATION OF PRIVILEGES OF REMOTE PILOTS WHO
ATTAIN THEIR SIXTIETH BIRTHDAY AND CURTAILMENT OF
PRIVILEGES OF REMOTE PILOTS WHO ATTAIN THEIR SIXTY-
FIFTH BIRTHDAY
(a) A Contracting State, having issued a remote pilot licence, will not
permit the holder thereof to act as pilot of a remotely piloted aircraft system
engaged in international commercial air transport operations if the licence
holder has attained his or her sixtieth birthday or, in the case of operations
with more than one pilot, his or her sixty-fifth birthday.
2.3.11.12 PRIVILEGES OF THE HOLDER OF THE REMOTE
PILOT LICENCE AND THE CONDITIONS TO BE OBSERVED IN
EXERCISING SUCH PRIVILEGES
(a) Subject to compliance with the requirements specified in Subsections
2.3.11.4 and 2.3.11.5 of this section, the privileges of the holder of a remote
pilot licenceshall be—

(1)  to act as remote Pilot-in-command of an remotely piloted aircraft
and associated remote pilot station, certificated for remote
single-pilot operation;

(2)  to act as remote co-pilot of an remotely piloted aircraft and
associated remote pilot station, required to be operated with a
remote co-pilot;

(3)  to act as a remote Pilot-in-command of an remotely piloted
aircraft and the associated remote pilot station, required to be
operated with a remote co-pilot; and

(4)  to act either as remote Pilot-in-command or as remote co-pilot
of a remotely piloted aircraft system under instrument flight
rules.
(b) Before exercising the privileges at night, the remote pilot licence
holder shall have received dual instruction in an remotely piloted aircraft and
associated remote pilot station in night flying, including take-off, landing,
and navigation.
Note: Certain privileges of the remote pilot licence are curtailed by
Subsection 2.3.11.11 of this section for remote pilot licence holders when
they attain their sixtieth and sixty-fifth birthdays.

2.3.11.13 REMOTELY PILOTED AIRCRAFT SYSTEM INSTRUCTOR
RATING
2.3.11.14 STUDENT REMOTE PILOT
(a) A student remote pilot shall meet requirements prescribed by the
Contracting State concerned. In prescribing such requirements, Contracting
States will ensure that the privileges granted would not permit student remote
pilots to constitute a hazard to air navigation.
(b) A student remote pilot shall not fly an remotely piloted aircraft
solo unless under the supervision of, or with the authority of, an authorised
remotely piloted aircraft system instructor.
(c) A student remote pilot shall not fly an remotely piloted aircraft solo
on international remotely piloted aircraft system operations unless by special
or general arrangement between the Contracting States concerned.
(d) Medical fitness.

(1)  A Contracting State will not permit a student remote pilot to
fly an remotely piloted aircraft solo unless that student holds a
current Class 3 or a current Class 1 medical certificate.
Note: A Class 1 medical certificate may be essential for a particular
individual based on their work environment and responsibilities in the context
of a specific remotely piloted aircraft system application.
2.3.11.15 REMOTE PILOT LICENCE
Note: The provisions of this section are for international instrument
flight rules operations of remotely piloted aircraft system.
2.3.11.16 REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ISSUE OF THE RATING
(a)  Knowledge.

(1)  The applicant shall demonstrate the ability to effectively assess
trainees against the adapted competency model used in the
approved training programme.

(2)  The applicant shall successfully complete the training and
meet the qualifications of an approved training organization
appropriate to the delivery of competency-based training
programmes.

(3)  The remotely piloted aircraft system instructor training
programme shall focus on the development of competence in
the following specific area—

(i)  the adapted competency model of the remote pilot training
programme according to the defined grading system used
by the remotely piloted aircraft system operator or approved
training organization;

(ii)  in accordance with the assessment and grading system of
the remotely piloted aircraft system operator or approved
training organization, making assessments by observing
behaviours; gathering objective evidence regarding the
observable behaviours of the adapted competency model
used;

(iii) recognising and highlighting performance that meets
competency standards;

(iv) determining root causes for deviations below the expected
standards of performance; and

(v)  identifying situations that could result in unacceptable
reductions in safety margins.
(4) The applicant shall have met the competency requirements for the
issue of a remote pilot licence as appropriate to the category of remotely
piloted aircraft and associated remote pilot station.
(5) In addition, the applicant shall have demonstrated a level of
competency appropriate to the privileges granted to the holder of a remotely
piloted aircraft system instructor rating, in at least the following areas —

(i)  techniques of applied instruction,

(ii)  assessment of student performance in those subjects in
which ground instruction is given,

(iii) the learning process,

(iv) elements of effective teaching,

(v)  competency-based training principles, including student
assessments,

(vi) evaluation of the training programme effectiveness,

(vii) lesson planning,

(viii) classroom instructional techniques,

(ix) use of training aids, including flight simulation training
devices, as appropriate,

(x)  analysis and correction of student errors,

(xi) human performance relevant to a remotely piloted aircraft
system, instrument, flight, and remote pilot licence training,
including principles of threat and error management, and

(xii) hazards involved in simulating system failures and
malfunctions in the aircraft.
(b) Skill.

(1)  The applicant shall have successfully performed a formal
competency assessment, prior to conducting instruction and
assessment within a competency-based training programme.

(2)  The competency assessment shall be conducted during a practical
training session in the category of remotely piloted aircraft
and associated remote pilot station for which an instructor
privileges are sought, including pre-flight, post-flight, and
ground instruction, as appropriate.

(3)  The competency assessment shall be conducted by a person
authorised by the Authority.
(c) Experience.

(1)  The applicant shall have met the requirements for the issue of
an remote pilot licence, shall maintain competencies, and shall
meet the recent experience requirements for the licence.

(2)  The applicant shall have sufficient training and experience
to attain the required level of proficiency in all the required
tasks, manoeuvres, operations and principles, and methods of
instruction relevant to Paragraph 2.3.11.16 (c) of this section.
(d) Remote pilot licence training.

(1)  The applicant shall, under the supervision of a remotely piloted
aircraft system instructor authorised by the Authority for that
purpose:

(i)  have received training in remotely piloted aircraft system
instructional techniques including demonstration, student
practices, recognition and correction of common student
errors, and

(ii)  have practiced instructional techniques in those flight
manoeuvres and procedures in which it is intended to
provide remote pilot licence training.

2.3.11.17 PRIVILEGES OF THE HOLDER OF THE RATING AND
THE CONDITIONS TO BE OBSERVED
(a) Subject to compliance with the requirements specified in subsection
2.11.1.8 of this section, the privileges of the holder of a remotely piloted
aircraft system instructor rating shall be —

(1) to supervise solo flights by student remote pilots; and

(2) to carry out remote pilot licence training for the issue of a
remote pilot licence and a remotely piloted aircraft system
instructor rating, provided that the remotely piloted aircraft
system instructor—

(i)  holds at least the a remote pilot licence and rating for which
instruction is being given, in the appropriate remotely
piloted aircraft category and associated remote pilot station,

(ii) holds the remote pilot licence and rating necessary to act
as the remote Pilot-in-command of the remotely piloted
aircraft category and associated remote pilot station on
which the instruction is given, and

(iii) has the remotely piloted aircraft system instructor privileges
granted endorsed on the remote pilot licence.
(b) The applicant, in order to carry out remote pilot licence training in
a multi-crew operational environment, shall have also met all the instructor
qualification requirements.

2.4  CERTIFICATION:  FLIGHT CREWMEMBERS OTHER THAN
PILOTS
2.4.1 Flight Engineers
2.4.1.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) This Section prescribes the requirements for issuing flight engineer
licences.
2.4.1.2  LICENCES AND RATINGS REQUIRED
(a)  A person shall not act as a flight engineer of a civil aircraft of Saint
Lucia registry unless he or she has a flight engineer licence with appropriate
ratings.

2.4.1.3  (RESERVED)
2.4.1.4  ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL
(a) To be eligible for a flight engineer licence, a person shall—

(1) be at least eighteen years of age;

(2) meet the English language proficiency requirements of Subsection
2.2.2 of this part; and

(3) comply with the requirements of this subsection that apply to
the rating sought.
2.4.1.5  ADDITIONAL AIRCRAFT RATINGS

(a) To add another aircraft class rating to a flight engineer licence, an
applicant shall —

(1) pass the knowledge test and skill test that is appropriate to the
class of aeroplane for which an additional rating is sought; or

(2) satisfactorily complete an approved flight engineer training
program that is appropriate to the additional class rating sought.
2.4.1.6  KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS
(a) An applicant for a flight engineer licence shall pass a knowledge
test on the following —

(1) the regulations that apply to a flight engineer;

(2) the theory of flight and aerodynamics;

(3) basic meteorology with respect to engine operations;

(4) centre of gravity computations.
(b) An applicant for the original or additional issue of a flight engineer
class rating shall pass a knowledge test for that aeroplane class on the
following —

(1) aeroplane equipment;

(2) aeroplane systems;

(3) aeroplane loading;

(4) aeroplane procedures and engine operations with respect to
limitations;

(5) normal operating procedures;

(6) emergency procedures.

(c) Before taking the knowledge tests prescribed in Paragraphs
2.4.1.6(a) and (b) of this subsection, an applicant for a flight engineer licence
shall present satisfactory evidence of having completed one of the experience
requirements of subsection 2.4.1.7 of this section.
(d) An applicant may take the knowledge tests before acquiring the
flight training required by Subsection 2.4.1.7 of this section.
(e) Except as provided in paragraph 2.4.1.6(f) of this subsection,
an applicant for a flight engineer licence or rating shall have passed the
knowledge tests required by Paragraphs 2.4.1.6(a) and (b) of this subsection
since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month in which
the skill test is taken.
(f) An applicant who within the period ending twenty-four calendar
months after passing the knowledge test, is employed as a flight crewmember
or mechanic by an Saint Lucia air carrier or certificate holder need not
comply with the time limit set in Paragraph 2.4.1.6(e) of this subsection if
the applicant —

(1) is employed by such a certificate holder at the time of the skill
test; and

(2) if employed as a flight crewmember, has completed initial
training, and, if appropriate, transition, upgrade, recurrent
training; or

(3) if employed as an aviation maintenance technician, meets the
recency of experience requirements of Part 5, subpart 5.6.
(g) An air operator certificate holder may, when authorised by the
Authority, provide as part of an approved training program a knowledge
test that it may administer to satisfy the test required for an additional rating
under Paragraph 2.4.1.6(b) of this subsection.
2.4.1.7 AERONAUTICAL EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS
(a) Except as otherwise specified herein, an applicant for a flight engineer
licence shall obtain and log the flight time used to satisfy the aeronautical
experience requirements of Paragraph 2.4.1.7(b) of this subsection on an
aeroplane on which a flight engineer is required by these regulations.
(b) An applicant for a flight engineer licence with a class rating shall
present, for the class rating sought, satisfactory evidence of one of the
following, including the practical experience with the aircraft described in
Paragraph 2.4.1.7(a) of this subsection —

(1)  at least three years of practical experience in aircraft and aircraft
engine maintenance and at least five hours of flight training in
the duties of a flight engineer;

(2) graduation from at least a two-year specialised aeronautical
training course in maintaining aircraft and aircraft engines and
at least five hours of flight training in the duties of a flight
engineer;

(3) a degree in aeronautical, electrical, or mechanical engineering
from a recognised college, university, or engineering school; at
least six calendar months of practical experience in maintaining
aircraft and at least five hours of flight training in the duties of
a flight engineer;

(4) at least a commercial pilot licence with an instrument rating
and at least five hours of flight training in the duties of a flight
engineer;

(5) at least two hundred hours of flight time in a transport category
aeroplane as Pilot-in-command or SIC performing the functions
of a Pilot-in-command under the supervision of a Pilot-in-
command;

(6) at least one hundred hours of flight time as a flight engineer;

(7) within the ninety-day period before application, successful
completion of an approved flight engineer ground and flight
course of instruction.
2.4.1.8  SKILL REQUIREMENTS
(a) An applicant for a flight engineer licence with a class and type
ratings shall pass a skill test on the  duties of a flight engineer in the class and
type of aeroplane for which a rating is sought only on an aeroplane specified in
Paragraph 2.4.1.7(a) of this section or an approved flight simulator replicating
the class and type of such an aeroplane.
(b)  An applicant shall—

(1) show satisfactory performance in pre-flight inspection, servicing,
starting, pre-take-off, and post landing procedures;

(2) in flight, show satisfactory performance of the normal duties
and procedures relating to the aeroplane, aeroplane engines,
propellers (if appropriate), systems, and appliances; and

(3) in flight, in an aeroplane simulator, or in an approved training
device, show satisfactorily performance on emergency duties
and procedures and recognise and take appropriate action
for malfunctions of the aeroplane, engines, propellers (if
appropriate), systems and appliances.
2.4.1.9  (RESERVED)
2.4.1.10 VALIDATION OF FOREIGN FLIGHT ENGINEERS
LICENCES AND RATINGS
(a) General. A person who holds a flight engineer’s licence issued by
another Contracting State may apply for a validation of that licence provided
that the applicant —

(1)  is not under an order of revocation or suspension by the country
that issued the pilot licence;

(2)  holds a licence that does not contain an endorsement stating
that the applicant has not met all of the standards of ICAO for
that licence;

(3)  does not currently hold a pilot licence issued by the Authority;

(4)  holds a current medical certificate issued by the country that
issued the applicant’s pilot licence;

(5)  meet the English language proficiency requirements of
Subsection 2.2.2 of this part;

(6)  the application must be supported by the relevant operator;

(7)  the licence must be current and contain the appropriate ratings
for the aircraft that the applicant intends to operate;

(8)  the licence to which this validation relates remains current
throughout the period of the validation
(b) Aircraft ratings issued. The Authority may validate the aircraft
ratings listed on that pilot’s foreign pilot licence.
(c) Operating privileges and limitations.  A person who is issued a
validation of a foreign pilot licence under the provisions of this subsection —

(1)  may act as a flight engineer of a civil aircraft of Saint Lucia
registry in accordance with the privileges authorised by this
Part;

(2)  shall be limited to the privileges placed on validation certificate
by the Authority;

(3)  shall be subject to the limitations and restrictions on the person’s
validation certificate issued by the Authority and foreign pilot
licence when exercising the privileges of that flight engineer’s
licence in an aircraft registered in Saint Lucia; and

(4)  shall not exercise the privileges of the validation issued by the
Authority when the person’s foreign flight engineer’s licence
has been revoked or suspended.
(d) Provisions for the validation of a foreign flight engineer’s licence —

(1)  an applicant may use only one foreign flight engineer’s licence
as a basis for obtaining a validation issued by the Authority;

(2)  an applicant for a validation under this subsection shall provide
a foreign flight engineer’s licence and medical certification in
the English language or accompanied by an English language
transcription that has been signed by an official or representative
of the foreign aviation authority that issued the foreign flight
engineer’s licence;

(3)  The Authory shall place on the validation certificate issued under
this Subsection the foreign flight engineer’s licence number and
country of issuance.
Implementing Standard: See Implementing Standard: 2.2.3 for details
on additional requirements and exemptions to the training requirements of
this subsection.
2.4.1.11 CONVERSION OF FOREIGN FLIGHT ENGINEERS
LICENCES AND RATINGS
(a) General.  A person who holds a current flight engineer’s licence
issued by another Contracting State may apply for a conversion of that licence
provided that —

(1) the applicant —

(i) is not under an order of revocation or suspension by the
Contracting State that issued the flight engineer’s licence,

(ii)  holds a licence that does not contain an endorsement stating
that the applicant has not met all of the standards of the
International Civil Aviation Organization for that licence,

(iii) does not currently hold a flight engineer’s licence issued
by the Authority;

(iv) holds a current medical certificate issued by the country
that issued the applicant’s pilot licence, and

(v)  meet the English language proficiency requirements of
subpart  2.2.2 of this regulation;

(2)  the application must be supported by the relevant operator;

(3)  thethat foreign flight engineer’s licence must be current and
contain the appropriate ratings for the aircraft that the applicant
intends to operate.
(b) Aircraft ratings issued. The Authority may convert the aircraft
ratings listed on that foreign flight engineer’s licence.
(c) Operating privileges and limitations.  A person who is issued a flight
engineer’s licence by the Authority based on the conversion of a foreign flight
engineer’s licence under the provisions of this subsection —

(1)  may act as a flight engineer of a civil aircraft of Saint Lucia
registration in accordance with the privileges authorised by this
part;

(2) shall be limited to the privileges placed on validation certificate,
if applicable, by the Authority;

(3)  shall be subject to the limitations and restrictions on the person’s
validation certificate, if applicable, issued by the Authority
and foreign pilot licence when exercising the privileges of that
foreign  engineer’s licence in an aircraft registered in Saint
Lucia.
(d) Provisions for the conversion of a foreign flight engineer’s licence —

(1)  an applicant may use only one foreign flight engineer’s licence as
a basis for obtaining a converted licence issued by the Authority;

(2) an applicant for a conversion under this subsection shall provide
a foreign flight engineer’s licence and medical certification in
the English language or accompanied by an English language
transcription that has been signed by an official or representative
of the foreign aviation authority that issued the foreign flight
engineer’s licence;

(3) an applicant for a conversion shall provide a passport to establish
age and nationality;

(4)  an applicant shall pass a Class I medical examination conducted
by an authorised medical examiner;

(5)  an applicant shall pass an examination in air law, flight rules
and procedures.

Implementing Standard: See Implementing Standard: 2.2.3 for details
on additional requirements and exemptions to the training requirements of
this subsection.

2.5  LICENSING:  AIRMEN OTHER THAN FLIGHT CREWMEMBERS
2.5.1 General
2.5.1.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) subpart 2.5 prescribes the requirements for issuing the following
licences, ratings, and inspection authorizations for —

(1)  air traffic controllers;

(2)  flight operations officers;

(3)  aviation maintenance technicians;

2.5.2
AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLERS
2.5.2.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) This subpart prescribes the requirements for issuance of student air
traffic controller licences, air traffic controller licences and ratings, and the
conditions under which those licences and ratings are necessary.
2.5.2.2  REQUIRED LICENCES, RATING OR QUALIFICATION
(a) A person shall not provide an air traffic controller service unless
he or she —

 (1) holds an air traffic controller licence issued to him or her under
this subpart;

(2) holds a holds a current air traffic controller rating;

(3)  maintains competency in accordance with criteria established
by the Authority; or

(4)  holds a student air traffic controller licence issued under this
subpart; and functions under the supervision of an appropriately
rated air traffic controller; or

(5)  is undergoing ab-initio departmental instruction from an air
traffic controller who is specifically authorized to carry out
instruction in an operational environment.

(b) The Authory shall take the appropriate measures to ensure that
student air traffic controllers do not constitute a hazard to air navigation.

2.5.2.3  ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS: GENERAL
(a) To be eligible for a student air traffic controller licence a person
shall —

(1)  be at least twenty-one years of age;

(2)  hold a Class three medical certificate issued under this part;

(3)  meet the English language proficiency requirements of Section
2.2.2 of this part; and

(4)  completed an approved training course covered in Subsection
2.5.2.4 of this section
(b) To be eligible for an air traffic controller licence a person shall —

(1)  be at least twenty-one years of age;

(2)  meet the English language proficiency requirements of Section
2.2.2 of this part;

(3)  meet the requirements of Subsection 2.5.2.4 of this section;
and

(4)  meet the requirements of at least one of the ratings set out in
Subsection 2.5.2.6 of this section
2.5.2.4 KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS
(a) An applicant for an air traffic controller licence shall have
demonstrated knowledge appropriate to the holder of an air traffic controller
licence in at least the following subjects—

(1)  Air law – Rules and regulations relevant to the air traffic
controller;

(2)  Air traffic control equipment – Principles, use and limitations
of equipment used in air traffic control;

(3)  General Knowledge - Principles of flight; principles of operation
and functioning of aircraft, power plants and systems; aircraft
performances relevant to air traffic control operations;

(4)  Human Performance - Human performance relevant to air traffic
control including principles of threat and error management;

(5)  Aeronautical meteorology; use and appreciation of meteorological
documentation and information; origin and characteristics of
weather phenomena affecting flight operations and safety;
altimetry;

(6)  Navigation - Principles of air navigation; principle, limitation
and accuracy of navigation systems and visual aids; and

(7)  Operational Procedures - Air traffic control, communication,
radiotelephony and phraseology procedures (routine, non routine
and emergency); use of the relevant aeronautical documentation;
safety practices associated with flight.
2.5.2.5  SKILL REQUIREMENTS
(a) An applicant for an Air Traffic Controller Licence shall pass a skill
test on the following —

(1)  safety of operation;

(2)  separation;

(3)  expedition and orderliness;

(4)  method and application of Air Traffic Procedures and Practices;

(5)  standard Chicago Convention phraseology;

(6)  co-ordination and communication;

(7)  correct use of equipment;

(8)  emergency and abnormal situations; and

(9)  impact of weather conditions on aircraft operations.
2.5.2.6  EXPERIENCE
(a) The applicant shall have completed an approved training course
and demonstrated the required competence, having accomplished not less
than three months of satisfactory service engaged in the actual control of
air traffic under the supervision of an air traffic control on the job training
instructor. The experience requirements specified for air traffic controller
ratings in Subsection 2.5.2.7 of this section may be credited as part of the
experience specified in this paragraph.
(b) An air traffic controller acting as an air traffic control on the job
training instructor shall hold an appropriate rating and be qualified as an air
traffic control on the job training instructor.

2.5.2.7  AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLER RATINGS AND
ENDORSEMENTS
(a) Air traffic controller ratings shall comprise the following categories
—

(1)  aerodrome control rating;

(2)  approach control procedural rating;

(3)  approach control surveillance rating;

(4)  approach precision radar control rating;

(5)  area control procedural rating; and

(6)  area control surveillance rating.
(b) Air traffic controller endorsements shall comprise the following
categories —

(1) Air Traffic Instructor Endorsement; and

(2)  Air Traffic Examiner Endorsement.
2.5.2.8  REQUIREMENTS FOR AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLER
RATINGS
(a) An applicant shall have demonstrated a level of knowledge
appropriate to the privileges granted in at least the following subjects in so
far as they affect the area of responsibility —
(b) Knowledge. The applicant for an air traffic controller rating shall
have received knowledge instruction through an approved training course
on the knowledge areas appropriate to the holder of an air traffic controller
rating on the subjects as specified below for each rating sought —

(1)  Aerodrome control rating —

(i)  aerodrome layout; physical characteristics and visual aids,

(ii)  airspace structure,

(iii) applicable rules, procedures, and source of information,

(iv) air navigation facilities,

(v)  air traffic control equipment and its use,

(vi) terrain and prominent landmarks,

(vii) characteristics of air traffic,

(viii) weather phenomena,

(ix) emergency and search and rescue plans.

(2)  Approach control procedural and area control procedural ratings
—

(i)  airspace structure —

(A) applicable rules, procedures, and source of information;

(B)  air navigation facilities;

(C)  air traffic control equipment and its use;

(D) terrain and prominent landmarks;

(E)  characteristics of air traffic and traffic flow;

(F)  weather phenomena;

(G) emergency and search and rescue plans;

(ii)  approach control surveillance, approach precision radar
control, and area control surveillance ratings—

(A) the applicant shall meet the requirements specified in
Paragraph 2.5.2.8(b)(2) of this subsection insofar as
they affect the area of responsibility, and shall have
demonstrated a level of knowledge appropriate to the
privileges granted, in at least the following additional
subjects;

(iii) principles, use, and limitations of applicable air traffic
service surveillance systems and associated equipment; and

(iv) procedures for the provision of air traffic service surveillance
services, as appropriate, including procedures to ensure
appropriate terrain clearance.
(c) Knowledge testing. The applicant for an air traffic controller rating
shall —

(1)  have received an endorsement for the knowledge test from an
authorised instructor who —

(i)  Conducted the training on the knowledge areas; and

(ii)  Certifies that the person is prepared for the required
knowledge test; and

(2)  pass the required knowledge test.

(d) Experience.

(1)  The applicant for an air traffic controller licence shall have —

(i) satisfactorily completed an approved training course;

(ii) demonstrated the required competence while providing,
under the supervision of an air traffic control on the job
training instructor, one or more of the following —

(A) Aerodrome control rating: an aerodrome control
service, for a period of not less than ninety hours or
one month, whichever is greater, at the unit for which
the rating is sought;

(B)  Approach control procedural, approach control
surveillance, area control procedural, or area control
surveillance rating: the control service for which the
rating is sought, for a period of not less than one
hundred and eighty hours or three months, whichever
is greater, at the unit for which the rating is sought;
and

(C)  Approach precision radar control rating: not less than
two hundred precision approaches of which not more
than one hundred shall have been carried out on a radar
simulator approved for that purpose by the Authority.
Not less than fifty of those precision approaches shall
have been carried out at the unit and on the equipment
for which the rating is sought; and

(2)  For the provision of Approach and Area Procedural control
services, the minimum initial training requirements shall be
Aerodrome, Approach and Area Procedural Control Service;

(3)  For the provision of Aerodrome Procedural Control Service,
the minimum initial training requirements shall be Aerodrome
and Approach Control Service;

(4)  For the provision Aerodrome Flight Information service, the
minimum initial training requirement shall be Aerodrome
Control Service;

(5) The application for a rating shall be made within six months from
the completion of experience specified in Paragraph 2.5.2.8(d)
(1)(ii) of this subsection.

(6) When the applicant already holds an air traffic controller rating
in another category or the same rating in another unit, the
Authority shall determine whether the experience requirements
of Paragraphs 2.5.2.8(c)(1) and (2) of this subsection may be
reduced and to what extent.
(e) Skill. The applicant shall have demonstrated, by passing the
required skill test, at a level appropriate to the privileges being granted, the
skill, judgement, and performance required to provide a safe, orderly, and
expeditious control service, including the recognition and management of
threats and errors.
(f) Concurrent issuance of two air traffic controller ratings. When two
air traffic controller ratings are sought concurrently, the Authority shall
determine the applicable requirements on the basis of the requirements for
each rating.  These requirements shall not be less than the those of the higher
rating.

2.5.2.9  CONVERSION OF AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLER LICENSES
(a) Conversion of air traffic controller licenses, which have been
verified in accordance with Subsection 2.5.2 of this part.

(1) the holder of a current and valid foreign air traffic control officer
licence issued by another Contracting State, in accordance with
ICAO Annex 1, may apply for conversion to the appropriate
licence and ratings issued by Saint Lucia, by submitting to the
Authority, the licence and a valid Class three medical Certificate
in support of the foreign licence.

(2) the applicant shall pass a Class three medical by an ECCAA
Aviation Medical Examiner.

(3) the authority may issue the applicant an air traffic control officer
Licence without ratings.

2.5.2.10 PRIVILEGES AND LIMITATIONS
(a)  Subject to compliance with the requirements specified in this part,
the privileges of the holder of an air traffic control officer licence with the
following applicable rating(s) shall be —

(1) aerodrome control rating: to provide or to supervise the provision
of aerodrome control service for the aerodrome for which the
licence holder is rated —

(i)  approach control procedural rating: to provide or to
supervise the provision of approach control service for
the aerodrome or aerodromes for which the licence holder
is rated, within the airspace or portion thereof, under the
jurisdiction of the unit providing approach control service,

(ii)  approach control surveillance rating: to provide and/or
supervise the provision of approach control service with the
use of applicable air traffic service surveillance systems for
the aerodrome or aerodromes for which the licence holder
is rated, within the airspace or portion thereof, under the
jurisdiction of the unit providing approach control service,

(iii) approach precision radar control rating: to provide and/or
supervise the provision of precision approach radar service
at the aerodrome for which the licence holder is rated,

(iv) area control procedural rating: to provide and/or supervise
the provision of area control service, within the control area
or portion thereof, for which the licence holder is rated,
and

(v)  area radar control surveillance rating: to provide and/or
supervise the provision of area control service with the
use of an air traffic service  surveillance system, within
the control area or portion thereof, for which the licence
holder is rated.

(2)  before exercising the privileges indicated in Paragraph 2.5.2.9(a)
(1), the licence holder shall be familiar with all pertinent and
current information;

(3)  a holder of an air traffic control officer licence and ratings(s)
shall not provide instruction in an operational environment
unless the licence holder has received proper authorization from
the Authority;

(4)  the holder of an air traffic controller licence shall not carry out
ab-initio instruction or instruct/supervise a non-rated controller
in an operational environment unless such holder has received
proper authorization from the Authority.

2.5.2.11 VALIDITY OF RATINGS.
(a) A rating shall become invalid when an air traffic controller has
ceased to exercise the privileges of the rating for a period determined by the
Authority. That period shall not exceed six months. A rating shall remain

invalid until the controller’s ability to exercise the privileges of the rating
has been re-established.
(b) An air traffic controller shall maintain currency of a rating by —

(1) exercising the privileges associated with a rating for at least
eight hours at each coordinating and control positions within
the preceding thirty days, of which at least five hours must be
done during a period when traffic volume and complexity are
appropriate to maintain competency; or

(2) successfully passing a competency evaluation assessment
conducted by an air traffic services examiner within the
preceding thirty days.
(c)  An air traffic controller who has not complied with Paragraph
2.5.2.10(b) of this subsection shall be removed from operational duties and
shall only be reinstated after —

(1) undergoing any coordinating and control retraining by the
air navigation service provider and has been assessed by an
air traffic services examiner to be competent to perform the
function and duties required for the required rating(s), or

(2) performed the coordinating and control functions and duties at
the aerodrome or in the airspace to which the rating relates,
under supervision of an on the job training instructor, for a
period determined by the Authority and has been assessed by
an air traffic services examiner to be competent to perform the
function and duties required for the required rating.

2.5.2.12 REST AND DUTY LIMITATIONS
(a) Except where the Authority determines that an emergency air traffic
situation has arisen, an air traffic controller shall have a minimum of twenty-
four consecutive hours free from duty within each seven consecutive days
of duty.
(b) Except where the Authority determines that an emergency air traffic
situation has arisen, an air traffic controller shall not work or be required to
work for more than twelve consecutive hours.
(c) An air traffic controller shall be required to take a rest period of at
least eight consecutive hours before each duty period.
(d) Notwithstanding Paragraph 2.5.2.11(c) of this subsection, where
the duty period is more than ten consecutive hours the rest period of the air
traffic controller shall be no less than the preceding duty period.

2.5.2.13 REQUIREMENT FOR ISSUE OF AIR TRAFFIC INSTRUCTOR
ENDORSEMENT
(a) An applicant for an air traffic instructor endorsement shall —

(1) apply to the Authority in the prescribed form;

(2) pay the fee;

(3) hold an air traffic controller licence issued in accordance with
this part with a rating for the relevant service;

(4) meet the English language proficiency requirements of Section
2.2.2 of this part;

(5) have at least three years experience as a senior air traffic
controller; and

(6) provide the Authority with evidence of having satisfactorily
completed an approved training course in the theory and practice
of instruction.
(b) Where an applicant meets the requirements of Paragraph 2.5.2.12 of
this subsection, the Authority may issue the air traffic instructor endorsement.
2.5.2.14 PRIVILEGES AND LIMITATIONS OF AIR TRAFFIC
CONTROLLER INSTRUCTOR ENDORSEMENT
(a) Subject to Paragraph 2.5.2.13(b) of this subsection, the holder of an
air traffic instructor endorsement (hereinafter referred to as “an Air Traffic
Instructor”) may —

(1)  instruct air traffic control personnel;

(2)  directly supervise air traffic control personnel undergoing
training or regaining recency or who are performing air traffic
control duties;

(3)  assess the preparedness of an applicant for the issue of an air
traffic controller licence or rating.
(b) Subject to Paragraph 2.5.2.13(d) of this subsection, an Air traffic
instructor in exercising the privileges under his endorsement shall hold a
current air traffic controller licence with a valid rating for the relevant service.
(c) Where Air Traffic Instructor is not exercising the privileges of an
air traffic controller licence, he is not required to hold a current medical
certificate.
(d) In exercising the privileges under Paragraph 2.5.2.13(a) of this
subsection, an air traffic instructor shall within the preceding thirteen months

have demonstrated to an air traffic examiner his ability to exercise such
privileges by passing an examination and a skill test based on the exercise
of such privileges.
2.5.2.15 REQUIREMENTS FOR AIR TRAFFIC EXAMINER
ENDORSEMENT
(a) An applicant for an Air Traffic Examiner Endorsement shall —

(1) have at least three years’ experience exercising the privileges
of an air traffic instructor or at least five years as a senior air
traffic controller, and is of good character;

(2)  apply to the Authority in the prescribed form;

(3)  pay the prescribed fee;

(4)  hold an air traffic controller licence issued in accordance with
this Part with a rating for the relevant service;

(5)  provide the Authority with evidence of having satisfactorily
completed an approved training course in the air traffic service
practical examination.
(b) An applicant who has met the criteria of Paragraph 2.5.2.14(a)(1)
to (5) of this subsection shall be designated by the Authority as an air traffic
examiner for aeronautical knowledge, skills and proficiency testing.
2.5.2.16  PRIVILEGES AND LIMITATIONS OF AIR TRAFFIC
EXAMINERS AUTHORIZATIONS
(a) Subject to Paragraph 2.5.2.15(b), the holder of an air traffic examiner
endorsement (hereinafter referred to as “an Air Traffic Examiner”) shall
conduct aeronautical knowledge and skill tests for initial issue or continued
validity of air traffic licences and ratings.
(b) An air traffic examiner in exercising the privileges of his air traffic
examiner authorization shall —

(1) hold a current air traffic service licence with a rating for the
relevant service;

(2) conduct the tests at an air traffic control facility or an aviation
training organization approved for air traffic control training;

(3) as far as practicable, not test an applicant to whom he has given
instruction for that licence or rating except with the expressed
consent in writing of the Authority.

2.5.2.17 AERODROME FLIGHT INFORMATION SERVICE
OFFICERS
(a) A person shall not provide an aerodrome flight information service
unless he or she has been authorized by the Authority.
(b) To be eligible for authorization to provide aerodrome flight
information service a person shall —

(1)  be at least eighteen years of age;

(2)  hold a Class three medical certificate issued under this part;

(3)  meet the English language proficiency requirements of Section
2.2.2; and

(4)  meet the requirements of Subsection 2.5.2.10 of this part.
2.5.2.18 REQUIREMENTS FOR AUTHORIZATION TO PROVIDE
AERODROME FLIGHT INFORMATION SERVICE
(a) Knowledge —

(1)  An applicant shall have demonstrated a level of knowledge
appropriate to aerodrome flight information service authorization
in at least the following subjects —

(i) rules of the Air  and air traffic procedures pertinent to
aerodrome operations;

(A) procedures and practices pertaining to flight information
service and alerting service;

(B)  terms used in the aeronautical mobile service to include
words and phrases and the phonetic alphabet;

(C)  communication codes and abbreviations used;

(D) radiotelephony phraseologies and operating procedures;

(E)  general air traffic services and airspace organization
within the State;

(F)  local aerodrome rules;

(G) characteristics of local traffic;

(H) local terrain and prominent landmarks;

(I)  local air navigation facilities;

(J)  procedures for coordination between the aerodrome
flight information service unit and its associated air
traffic control unit;

(K) pertinent data regarding meteorological reports and
effect of significant weather characteristics; and

(L)  local procedures for alerting of emergency services.
(b) Experience

(1)  the applicant shall have satisfactorily;

(i)  completed an approved aerodrome control course, and

(ii) provided Aerodrome Flight Information Service at that
aerodrome flight information service unit under the
supervision of an authorized aerodrome flight information
service officer or an appropriately rated air traffic controller
for not less than two months.
(c) Skill

(1)  The applicant shall have demonstrated competency in —

(i)  the manipulation and operation of typical transmit/receiver
equipment and controls, including ancillary facilities and
radio direction-finding apparatus in use;

(ii)  the visual inspection and daily operational check of the
radio equipment in use;

(iii) the transmission of radiotelephony messages, including
correct microphone technique, enunciation, and speech
quality; and

(iv) the reception of telephony messages and the ability to relay
messages correctly
2.5.3
Flight Operations Officer
2.5.3.1  APPLICABILITY
(a)  This subpart prescribes the requirements for the issue, renewal, and
reissue of a flight operations officer licence, instructors for flight operations
officer licences, and designation of flight operations officer examiner.
2.5.3.2  GENERAL
(a) An applicant shall, before being issued a flight operations officer
licence, meet such requirements with respect to age, knowledge, experience,

skill, medical fitness, and language proficiency as are specified for that
licence.
(b) An applicant shall, for renewal or reissue of a licence, meet the
requirements as are specified for that licence.
(c) An applicant shall demonstrate the ability to read, write, speak,
and understand the language of Saint Lucia, and English if required by the
Authority.
2.5.3.3  FLIGHT OPERATIONS OFFICER LICENCE - GENERAL
REQUIREMENTS
(a) Age. The applicant for a flight operations officer licence shall be
at least twenty-one years of age.
(b) Knowledge. The applicant for a flight operations officer  licence
shall receive and log training from an authorised instructor on the following
subjects appropriate to the privileges of the flight operations officer —

(1) Air law

(i)  rules and regulations relevant for operational control and
to the holder of a flight operations officer licence,

(ii)  appropriate air traffic service practices and procedures;

(2)  Aircraft general knowledge

(i)  principles of operation of aeroplane power plants, systems,
and instruments;

(ii)  operating limitations of aeroplanes and power plants;

(iii) minimum equipment list and configuration deviation list;

(3)  Flight performance calculation, planning procedures, and
loading.

(i)  effects of loading and mass distribution on aircraft
performance and flight characteristics; mass and balance
calculations —

(A) operational flight planning; fuel consumption and
endurance calculations; alternate aerodrome selection
procedures; en route cruise control; extended range
operation;

(B)  take-off performance including field length, climb, and
obstacle criteria and limitation;

(C)  cruise performance including minimum altitudes,
decompression/engine out/gear down scenario
planning;

(D) landing performance including approach climb and
field length criteria and limitations;

(E)  preparation and filing of air traffic service flight plans;

(F) basic principles of computer-assisted planning systems.

(4)  Human performance

(i) human performance relevant to operational control duties,
including principles of threat and error management;

(5)  Meteorology

(i)  aeronautical meteorology; the movement of pressure
systems; the structure of fronts, and the origin and
characteristics of significant weather phenomena which
affect take-off, en route, and landing conditions —

(A) interpretation and application of aeronautical
meteorological reports, charts, and forecasts; codes and
abbreviations; use of, and procedures for obtaining,
meteorological information;

(6)  Navigation

(i)  principles of air navigation with particular reference to
instrument flight;

(7)  Operational procedures

(i)  use of aeronautical documentation and standard operating
procedures —

(A) operational procedures for the carriage of freight and
dangerous goods;

(B)  procedures relating to aircraft accidents and incidents;
emergency flight procedures;

(C) procedures relating to unlawful interference and
sabotage of aircraft;

(8)  Principles of flight

(i)  principles of flight relating to the appropriate category of
aircraft; and

(9)  Radiotelephony

(i)  procedures for communicating with aircraft and relevant
ground stations.
(c) Knowledge testing. The applicant for a fight operations officer
licence shall —

(1) have received an endorsement for the knowledge test from an
authorised instructor who —

(i)  conducted the training on the knowledge areas; and

(ii) certifies that the person is prepared for the required
knowledge test; and

(2)  pass the required knowledge test.
(d) Experience

(1) The applicant for a fight operations officer licence shall have —

(i)  a total of two years of service in any one or in any
combination of the capacities specified in Paragraphs
2.5.3.3(d)(1)(i)(A) to (C) of this subsection, inclusive,
provided that in any combination of experience the period
serviced in any capacity shall be at least one year —

(A) a flight crew member in air transportation; or

(B)  a meteorologist in an organization providing operational
control to aircraft in air transportation; or

(C)  an air traffic control officer, or a technical supervisor
of a fight operations officer or air transportation flight
operations systems; or

(ii)  at least one year as an assistant in the dispatching of air
transport, or

(iii) satisfactorily completed a course of approved training.

(2)  The applicant shall have served under the supervision of a flight
operations officer for at least ninety working days within the
six months immediately preceding the application.
(e) SKILL. The applicant shall have demonstrated the ability, by passing
a skill test on the areas of operation in the ECCAA skill test standards for a
flight operations officer to —

(1)  identify and to retrieve aeronautical data and other information
relevant for the analysis of operational situations and risks;

(2)  identify and evaluate the risk factors and the possible
consequences for flight operations;

(3)  identify and evaluate actions considering risk, the effect on
flight safety and regularity of the operation;

(4)  determine an appropriate course of action based on the
responsibilities and policies described in the operations manual;

(5)  apply appropriate standard and non-standard procedures from
the operations manual for the initiation, planning, continuation,
diversion, or termination of flights in the interest of safety of
the aircraft and regularity and efficiency of the operation;

(6)  make an accurate and operationally acceptable weather analysis;
provide an operationally valid briefing on weather conditions
of a specific air route; forecast weather trends pertinent to
air transportation with particular reference to destination and
alternates;

(7)  identify and apply operational limitations and minimums
in relation to the weather, aircraft status, and appropriate
navigation procedures;

(8)  determine the optimum flight path for a given segment and
create accurate manual and/or computer-generated flight plans;

(9)  provide operating supervision and all other assistance to a flight
in actual or simulated adverse weather conditions, as appropriate
to the duties of the holder of a flight operations officer licence;
and

(10) recognise and manage threats and errors.
(f) Privileges. Subject to compliance with the requirements specified
in this part, the privileges of the holder of a flight operations officer licence
shall be to serve in that capacity with responsibility for each area for which
the applicant meets the Standards specified in ICAO Annex 6, as contained
in Parts 8 and 9 of these regulations.
(g) Validity. The validity period of the licence is one year. A licence
shall become invalid when a flight operations officer has ceased to exercise
the privileges of the licence for a period of six months. A licence shall remain
invalid until the flight operations officer’s ability to exercise the privileges
of the licence has been re-established.
(h) Renewal. The  flight operations officer licence may be renewed by
presenting to the Authority evidence of successfully passing a competency

check on the areas of operation listed in the ECCAA skill test standards for
a flight operations officer.
(i) Reissue. If a flight operations officer licence has expired, the
applicant shall have received refresher training acceptable to the Authority,
and shall pass a skill test on the areas of operation contained in the ECCAA
skill test standards for a flight operations officer.
2.5.3.4  SKILL TEST FOR THE FLIGHT OPERATIONS OFFICER
LICENCE
(a) The ECCAA skill test standards for a flight operations officer
contain the list of operations included in the flight operations officer licence
skill test.
2.5.4
Instructors for Flight Operations Officers
2.5.4.1  REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FLIGHT OPERATIONS
OFFICER INSTRUCTOR LICENCE
(a) Age. An applicant for a flight operations officer nstructor licence
and rating shall be at least twenty one years of age.
(b) Knowledge

(1)  An applicant for an flight operations officer instructor licence
shall have met the instructor requirements in Section 2.2.6 of
this part; and

(2)  Any additional requirements, as may be specified by the
Authority.
(c) Experience  The applicant for a flight operations officer instructor
licence shall hold at least a current and valid flight operations officer licence
and shall have a minimum of three years of experience as a flight operations
officer.
(d) Privileges. The privileges of a flight operations officer instructor
licence are to give instruction to a flight operations officer licence applicants
and to endorse those applicants for a knowledge or skill test, as applicable.
(e) Validity. Subject to compliance with the requirements specified in
this part, the validity period of the flight operations officer instructor licence
is two years.

(f) renewal. A flight operations officer instructor licence that has not
expired may be renewed for an additional twenty-four calendar months if
the holder presents to the Authority evidence that he or she has, within the
past twelve months preceding the expiry date —

(1) conducted at least six exercises in an approved course for a flight
operations officer licence; or

(2)  received refresher training acceptable to the Authority.
(g) Reissue. If  a flight operations officer instructor licence has expired,
the applicant shall have received refresher training acceptable to the Authority.
2.5.5
Designated Examiners for Flight Operations Officers
2.5.5.1  GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
(a) Age. The applicant for a flight operations officer examiner shall be
at least twenty-three years of age.
(b) General eligibility. The applicant for a flight operations officer
examiner shall —

(1)  show evidence of a high level of aeronautical knowledge in the
subject areas for a flight operations officer certification;

(2)  have held a flight operations officer licence for at least five years
prior to the designation;

(3)  have been actively exercising the privileges of a flight operations
officer licence in commercial air transport in the previous three
years;

(4)  have a good record as a flight operations officer and as a person
engaged in the industry and community, with a reputation for
honesty and dependability;

(5)  have satisfactorily completed the flight operations officer
examiner orientation programme with the Authority; and

(6)  have available a test site that is fully capable of doing all items
required for the proper dispatch of a commercial flight in
accordance with the regulatory requirements. This may be the
flight operations office of an active commercial airline.

2.5.5.2  KNOWLEDGE
(a) The applicant shall have passed a pre-designation test on the
following —

(1) air law and regulations for a flight operations officer personnel;

(2) aircraft knowledge on the aircraft used for testing;

(3) flight performance calculation and planning procedures;

(4) human performance;

(5) meteorology;

(6) navigation;

(7) radio communication; and

(8) recent changes in technology, to include fly-by-wire aircraft
systems, global positioning system navigation, required
navigation performance requirements, traffic alert and collision
avoidance system, automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast,
and enhanced wind shear systems.
2.5.5.3  SKILL
(a) The Authory shall observe the applicant conducting a complete,
actual flight operations officer certification using the approved skill test
standard in a satisfactory manner.
(b) The applicant shall complete all required paperwork for the
certification as required by the Authority.
2.5.5.4  CURRENCY
(a) After designation, a flight operations officer examiner shall maintain
currency by —

(1) attending initial and recurrent training conducted by the Authority;
and

(2) maintaining a current and valid flight operations officer licence.
(b) The flight operations officer examiner shall conduct at least six skill
tests during any twelve calendar month period in order for the designation
to remain current.
(c) The flight operations officer examiner shall be observed by the
Authority in the conduct of a skill test at least once every twelve calendar
months.

 2.5.5.5  PRIVILEGES
(a) The flight operations officer examiner may conduct skill tests for
the flight operations officer licence in accordance with approved skill test
standard standards.
(b) The flight operations officer examiner may conduct or monitor any
portion of a computerised knowledge test.
2.5.5.6  VALIDITY
(a) The flight operations officer examiner licence shall be valid for
three years.
2.5.5.7  RENEWAL
(a) The flight operations officer examiner designation may be renewed
by the Authority if —

(1) the need for the designation remains valid; and

(2) the performance of the examiner has been satisfactory.
2.5.6  Aviation Maintenance Technicians
Note:  The terms “licenced Engineer,” “aviation maintenance engineer”
or “aircraft maintenance engineer”may be used instead of “Aviation
Maintenance Technician”
2.5.6.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) This Section prescribes the requirements for issuance of an aviation
maintenance technician licence and associated ratings which are issued and
extended within the defined Categories given in Subsection 2.5.6.3 of this
section.
(b) There are two parts to each Category—

(1) Licence Without Type Rating. This licence does not confer
any certification responsibilities or privileges. It is, however,
a prerequisite for the grant of the relevant Type Ratings and
Certification Authorization within an approved maintenance
organization;

(2) type Ratings. Type Ratings confer on the holder of a Licence
Without Type Rating the privileges and certification
responsibilities defined in Subsection 2.5.6.7 of this section.

2.5.6.2  ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS:  GENERAL
(a) An applicant for the grant / extension of a licence shall —

(1) submit an application which is acceptable in content and
presentation;

(2) provide evidence of acceptable experience required by
Implementing Standard 2.5.6.5 and any training course
requirements relevant to the application;

(3) comply with the knowledge and competency requirements
prescribed for the rating sought;

(4) be able to read, write, interpret technical reports and carry out
technical discussions in the English language;

(5) pass all of the prescribed tests for the rating sought;

(6) pay the appropriate fee.
(b) An applicant for the conversion of a Licence based on a licence or
certificate not issued by Saint Lucia shall —

(1) submit an application which is acceptable in content in type and
form;

(2)  enclose original documents or acceptable certified copies of the
licences and certificates supporting the application;

(3)  be able to read, write, interpret technical reports and carry out
technical discussions in the English language;

(4)  pay the appropriate fee.
Implementing Standard: See Implementing Standard 2.5.6.2 for further
requirements and procedures for the acceptance of foreign licences and
certificates.
2.5.6.3  RATINGS
(a) Categories and Ratings defined in Implementing Standard: 2.5.6.3
are issued under this subpart.
2.5.6.4  AIRCRAFT RATING:  KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS
(a) An applicant for an aviation maintenance technician licence or rating
shall, after meeting the applicable experience requirements of Subsection
2.5.6.5 of this Part, pass the applicable –

(1) knowledge tests covering the construction and maintenance of
aircraft appropriate to the category and rating sought;

(2) the regulations; and

(3) the provisions of the applicable Parts.
(b) The examination for the grant of a Licence will normally be in
two parts —

(1) a written examination, comprising a multi-choice question paper
and an essay question paper; and

(2)  an oral examination.
(c) All papers of the written examination must be taken at one sitting.
(d) The oral examination can only be taken after the written examination
has been passed and normally must be taken within three months of the
written examination.
(e) The applicant shall pass each section of the written test before
completing any necessary oral examination.
Implementing Standard; See Implementing Standard 2.5.6.4 for details
of the examinations, the examination syllabus and procedures following
partial passes.
2.5.6.5  EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS
(a) Applications for the grant or extension of an aviation maintenance
technician licence in any category must demonstrate compliance with the
experience requirements detailed in Implementing Standard: 2.5.6.5.

2.5.6.6  SKILL REQUIREMENTS
(a) Each applicant for an aviation maintenance technician licence or
rating must pass an oral and a skill test on the rating he seeks. The tests cover
the applicant’s basic skill in performing practical projects on the subjects
covered by the written test for that rating.
(b) A skill test is not required provided the experience requirement of
Subsection 2.5.6.5 of this section is satisfied.
2.5.6.7  PRIVILEGES AND LIMITATIONS
(a) A licenced aviation maintenance technician may perform or
supervise the maintenance, or modification of, or after inspection, approve for
return to service, any aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance,
component, or part thereof, for which he or she has a valid appropriately
type rated licence.

(b) A licenced aviation maintenance technician in Category ‘A’ with the
appropriate type rating may, after he or she has performed the one hundred
hour or annual inspection required by Part 8 of these regulations on an
airframe, or any related part or appliance, approve it for return to service.
(c) A licenced aviation maintenance technician in Category ‘C’ with
the appropriate type rating may, after he or she has performed the one
hundred1 hour or annual inspection required by Part 8 of these regulations
on a powerplant or propeller, or any related part or appliance, approve for
return to service.
(d) A licenced aviation maintenance technician in any Category shall
not —

(1) approve for return to service any aircraft, airframe, aircraft
engine, propeller, appliance, component, or part thereof which
is operated on an air operator certicate issued in accordance
with Part 9 of these regulations unless he or she is approved
by the approve maintenance organization  responsible for the
maintenance and listed in the list of certifying staff;

(2) exercise the privileges of the licence unless the aviation
maintenance technician understands the current instructions
for continued airworthiness and the maintenance instructions
for the specific operation concerned;

(3)  perform or supervise —

(i)  a major repair or major modification of a propeller, or

(ii)  any repair or alteration of instruments;

(4) approve for return to service —

(i)  any aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance,
component, or part thereof after completion of a major
alteration or major repair, or

(ii)  any instrument after completion of any repair or alteration.

2.5.6.8  (RESERVED)
2.5.6.9  (RESERVED)
2.5.6.10 AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN LICENCE
RENEWAL
(a) It is the responsibility of the Licence holder to ensure that his or
her Licence remains valid.
(b) An applicant for the renewal of a licence shall —

(1) submit an application for renewal which is acceptable in form
and content;

(2) provide evidence of having been engaged on the maintenance of
operating aircraft for periods of at least six months during the
twelve months before application for renewal;

(3) where a Licence holder is unable to show such experience, as
required by Paragraph 2.5.6.10(b)(2), but has been actively
involved for the same periods in matters concerned with aircraft
maintenance, such as a quality engineer or quality manager,
an aeronautical engineering instructor or as a flight engineer,
consideration will be given to renewing the Licence;

(4) pay the appropriate fee.
(c) Expired Licences —

(1)  a Licence which has lapsed for less than two years may be
considered for renewal without examination of the holder
provided that the requirements of Paragraph 2.5.6.10(b) and
the implementing standards are met;

(2)  a Licence which has lapsed for more than two years may not
be renewed without examination of the holder. The amount of
recent experience required may depend on the length of time
the since the Licence lapsed and the nature of employment.
2.5.7
Certification Authorizations
2.5.7.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) This subpart prescribes the requirements for issuance of certification
authorizations, and the conditions under which these authorizations are
necessary.

2.5.7.2  ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS:  GENERAL
(a) An approved maintenance organization shall issue a Certification
Authorization to Certifying Staff in accordance with procedures approved by
the Authority. Such procedures shall contain at least the following eligibility
requirements —

(1) the applicant must hold a valid aircraft maintenance technician
licence without type rating  issued by the Authority or an
appropriate validation of a foreign licence in the appropriate
category;

(2) the applicant must have completed an appropriate type course
approved by the Authority or hold the appropriate Type Rating;

(3) the applicant must pass an examination on the approved
maintenance organization procedures;

(4) the applicant must submit to the approved maintenance
organization, a satisfactory record of experience as specified
in Subsection 2.5.6.5 of this section.
2.5.8
(Reserved)
2.6
MEDICAL PROVISIONS FOR LICENSING
2.6.1
General
2.6.1.1  APPLICABILITY
(a) This subpart prescribes the requirements and procedures for issuing
and reissuing Class 1, Class 2, and Class three medical certificates.
(b) The medical assessment process of licence holders shall include
basic safety management principles in its —

(1) routine analysis of in-flight incapacitation events and medical
findings during medical assessments to identify areas of
increased medical risk; and

(2) continuous re-evaluation of the medical assessment process to
concentrate on identified areas of increased medical risk.
(c) The Authority will implement appropriate aviation-related health
promotion for licence holders subject to a medical assessment to reduce future
medical risks to flight safety.
Note: Paragraph 2.6.1.1(b) of this subsection indicates how appropriate
topics for health promotion activities may be determined.

2.6.1.2  MEDICAL FITNESS
(a) An applicant for a flight crew licence or air traffic controller license
shall hold a medical certificate issued in accordance with this Part.
(b) The flight crew members or air traffic controllers shall not exercise
the privileges of their licence unless they hold a current medical certificate
appropriate to the licence.
(c) The period of validity of a medical certificate shall begin on the day
the medical examination is performed. The duration of the period of validity
shall be in accordance with the provisions of subsection 2.6.2.4 of this section
(d) The period of validity of a medical certificate may be extended, at
the discretion of the Authority up to forty-five days.
(e) The period of validity of a medical certificate may be reduced when
clinically indicated.

2.6.1.3  AVIATION MEDICAL EXAMINERS
(a) Subject to compliance with the requirements specified in this Part,
the Authority will designate and authorise qualified and licensed physicians
in the practice of medicine, to be authorised as an aviation medical examiner
and to conduct medical examinations of fitness of applicants for the issue,
renewal or re-issue of the licences or ratings specified in this Part. An aviation
medical examiner may be designated outside of Saint Lucia.
(b) Aviation medical examiners shall have had training in Basic and
Advanced aviation medicine.  Before designation, medical examiners shall
demonstrate adequate competency in aviation medicine.
(c) Aviation medical examiners shall receive refresher training every
three years;
(d) Aviation medical examiners shall have practical knowledge and
experience of the conditions in which the holders of licences and ratings
carry out their duties.
Note:  Examples of practical knowledge and experience are flight
experience, simulator experience, on-site observation or any other hands-on
experience deemed by the Authority to meet this requirement.
(e) The authorization of an aviation medical examiner is valid for three
years.  Re-authorization will be at the discretion of the Authority
(f) Having completed the medical examination of an applicant in
accordance with this Section, the aviation medical examiner shall submit a
signed report to the Authority detailing the results of the examination.

(g) Medical confidentiality shall be respected at all times.
(h) All medical reports and records shall be securely held with
accessibility restricted to authorized personnel.
(i) If the medical examination is carried out by a constituted group
of aviation medical examiners, the head of the group will be appointed by
the Authority, who will be responsible for coordinating the results of the
examination and signing the report.

(j) An aviation medical examiner shall report to the Authority any
individual case where, in the examiner’s judgement, an applicant’s failure
to meet any requirement could jeopardise flight safety.
(k) The Authority shall use the services of physicians experienced in
the practice of aviation medicine, when it is necessary to evaluate reports
submitted to the Authority by medical examiners.
(l) The Authority retains the right to reconsider any action of an aviation
medical examiner.

2.6.1.4  AVIATION MEDICAL EXAMINATIONS
(a) Applicants for licences or ratings for which medical fitness is
prescribed shall sign and furnish to the aviation medical examiner a declaration
stating whether they have previously undergone such an examination and, if
so, the date, place and results of the last examination.
(b) The applicant shall indicate to the medical examiner whether a
medical certificate has previously been refused, revoked, or suspended and,
if so, the reason for such refusal, revocation, or suspension.
(c) Each applicant for a medical certificate shall provide the aviation
medical examiner with a personally certified statement of medical facts
concerning personal, familial and hereditary history.

(d) Each applicant for a medical certificate shall produce proof of
identification.
(e) Any false declaration to an aviation medical examiner made by an
applicant for a licence or rating shall be reported to the Authority for such
action as may be considered appropriate.
(f) The applicant shall complete the appropriate form as prescribed by
the Authority.

2.6.1.5  SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES
